content.title: NASA's first Moon mission since 1972 finishes with 'perfect' descent to Earth — as it happened
content.text: The Artemis II crew has returned to Earth, splashing down in the Pacific Ocean in a "perfect bullseye".The four NASA astronauts travelled further from Earth than any humans before, surpassing the record set by Apollo 13 in 1970.Read back over the day's event in our live blog.Key EventsSat 11 AprSat 11 Apr 2026 at 3:31amSat 11 AprSat 11 Apr 2026 at 1:35amSat 11 AprSat 11 Apr 2026 at 1:31amSat, 12:23amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 12:23amWelcome to our live coverageSat, 7:11amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 7:11amWe're going to leave it thereBy Dannielle MaguireThanks for joining us today!Be sure to check in again tomorrow for updates on the crew and the recovery mission.The mission might be over but there's still plenty more to come!(NASA: Bill Ingalls)Sat, 7:05amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 7:05amMore photos from the flight deckBy Dannielle MaguireSat, 6:00amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 6:00amWhere did you watch the splashdown from?By Dannielle MaguireThe broadcast was on the big screens here in the ABC office and at the home of the New York Mets baseball team.Sat, 4:52amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 4:52amWho are the Artemis II astronauts?By Dannielle MaguireThere were four crew members on the Artemis II mission.Commander: Reid WisemanPilot: Victor GloverMission specialist: Christina KochMission specialist: Jeremy HansenIt was Wiseman, Koch and Glover's second time in space.It was Hansen's first space flight.Want to find out more about the crew? We have a great wrap here.Sat, 4:41amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 4:41amTrump congratulates crew in social media postBy Dannielle MaguireUS President Donald Trump has posted about the splashdown on his social media platform, Truth Social:"Congratulations to the Great and Very Talented Crew of Artemis II."The entire trip was spectacular, the landing was perfect and, as President of the United States, I could not be more proud!"I look forward to seeing you all at the White House soon."We'll be doing it again and then, next step, Mars!"Sat, 4:36amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 4:36amPHOTOS: Big grins on deckBy Dannielle MaguireNASA has posted some happy snaps of the crew after they were brought aboard the USS John P Murtha.We saw some grainy overhead footage of those moments, but these pictures from the flight deck are much, much clearer.Victor Glover and Christina Koch. (NASA: Bill Ingalls)Reid Wiseman and Jeremy Hansen (NASA: Bill Ingalls)Jeremy Hansen, (NASA: Bill Ingalls)Sat, 4:14amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 4:14amIn photos: How the US Navy prepped for the Orion's returnBy Dannielle MaguireHere are a few snaps from USS John P Murtha in the days leading up to Orion's return to Earth.The crew were taken to the USS Murtha after landing in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of southern California.US Navy personnel made up the recovery teams who greeted the astronauts and brought them safely to the ship.(NASA: Joel Kowsky)(NASA: Joel Kowsky)(NASA: Joel Kowsky)Sat, 4:03amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 4:03amArtemis II crew entering Earth's atmosphere, as seen from International Space StationBy Annabel BowlesChris Williams, a NASA astronaut on the International Space Station, snapped these images of the Orion spacecraft as it hurtled back towards Earth this morning.You can see a wispy trail the capsule left behind in the upper atmosphere.Sat, 3:52amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 3:52amKatherine Bennell-Pegg describes how Australia contributed to epic missionBy Annabel BowlesAstronaut and Australian of the Year Katherine Bennell-Pegg says it was a thrill watching Artemis II splash down off the Californian coast with her two daughters, knowing she and Australia had contributed towards the mission.Bennell-Pegg is the director of space technology at the Australian Space Agency and lives in Adelaide.(ABC News)She said she was "so happy" to cheer on the astronaut as they came back to Earth."My kids said, 'Oh my goodness, will you do that?' and I said, 'Maybe, we'll see.' I've certainly trained for it, and what a ride it would be, and it was wonderful to share in that with them," Bennell-Pegg said.Bennell-Pegg was one of thousands of engineers who contributed to the mission.(ABC News)More specifically, Australia contributed through the European Space Agency's service module at the back of the spacecraft.Bennell-Pegg said Australia's future contributions include the 20kg moon Roo-ver, the SPIDER seismic wave tester, greenhouses and sensors."All of this is going to bring jobs and economic growth back here, too, and I hope to help our kids look up in awe and not just at other nations' achievements but at what's happening right here in Australia and what their future might hold, too," she said.Reporting by Eugene BoisvertSat, 3:31amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 3:31amFirst images of space crew's splashdownBy Annabel BowlesNASA has published its first images of the Artemis II crew's splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, and they are stunning.(NASA/Bill Ingalls)(NASA/Bill Ingalls)We can also see NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman being greeted by Navy sailors onboard USS John P Murtha, ahead of the astronauts' return.(NASA/Bill Ingalls)(NASA/Bill Ingalls)Sat, 3:09amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 3:09amArtemis III mission is 'right around the corner'By Dannielle MaguireNASA was asked about planning for the next mission.Artemis II Flight Director Rick Henfling didn't give any specifics on that front:"The next mission is right around the corner."We'll take the lessons learned from Artemis II"We learned a bunch on how to fly people in space, both from a vehicle operations, but also from how to how to run a control room with a deep space mission."And when the time is right, we'll get back into flight specific training."Sat, 3:05amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 3:05amHow will the heat shield be assessed?By Dannielle MaguireThere's been a lot of talk about the heat shield after there were unexpected issues in the Artemis I mission.Artemis II had the same heat shield but re-entered Earth's atmosphere in a different way, so people are keen to see how that went this time around.Lori Glaze says NASA will be paying close attention to that, with divers taking imagery of the heat shield while it was still in the water.Here's more from Orion program manager Howard Hu:"When we get the crew module into the well deck [we] will do some inspections right off the bat."We'll capture a lot of great imagery and obviously we have not had time to digest all that data but we will in the next several days."We will make sure we understand if there is anything that happened that was anomalous."Sat, 2:51amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 2:51amWhen will the crew of Artemis III be announced?By Dannielle MaguireSoon, NASA says.But they refused to be any more specific than that.Sat, 2:48amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 2:48amOrion being plucked from the oceanBy Dannielle MaguireNASA says the crew capsule is being recovered from the ocean as we speak."Our recovery teams are currently in the process of bringing Orion back."Hopefully in about four or five hours it will be in the back end of the USS Murtha."Sat, 2:43amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 2:43amNASA: 'Ya'll, we did it'By Dannielle MaguireNASA's Lori Glaze is clearly stoked with how things went today."Ya'll, we did it."We sent four amazing people to the moon and safely returned them to Earth for the first time in more than 50 years."To that generation that now knows what we are capable of, welcome to our moonshot."Sat, 2:38amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 2:38amNASA is giving a press conference nowBy Dannielle MaguireWe'll bring you updates from the media room in Houston in the US state of Texas.Sat, 2:37amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 2:37amVIDEO: Astronauts walk from choppersBy Dannielle Maguire The four Artemis II crew members — Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen and Reid Wiseman — were able to walk from the recovery choppers to the medical bay.Artemis II crew takes first steps on recovery ship, the USS John P MurthaSat, 2:29amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 2:29amNASA's broadcast has endedBy Dannielle MaguireIf you had the NASA livestream open on YouTube, chances are something else is playing now (the autoplay feature took me to a two-hour soundscape apparently inspired by the Shire in Lord of the Rings...).But there still is more to come.We're going to be hanging around waiting for more updates from the crew, NASA's pictures from the splashdown and hopefully a press conference.So stay with us!Sat, 2:26amSat 11 Apr 2026 at 2:26amCrew were all smiles after splashdownBy Dannielle MaguireI don't know about you, but bobbing around in the ocean for more than an hour after nine days in space doesn't sound like much fun to meBut that didn't seem to bother the Artemis crew.Artemis II landing and recovery director Liliana Villarreal said the mood aboard the Orion was good:"When we opened the hatch, they were already out of their seats, having a good time, waiting for us to open the hatch."They were just having such a great time with the medical team that was inside the capsule."I think they were all taking selfies with the phones that they had."Probably talking about what they saw, and it was just... there were just smiles all around."They were having such a great time."And then we put them on the front porch when we were ready to put them on the front porch, and again, you could just see that they were so ecstatic to be home and talking to everybody."This post previously attributed the above quotes to Sawyer Rosenstein and has been amended to correct the error.
